question.text: Who must you yield to at crossings and private-road entries?

answer.text: Yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks or at unmarked intersections. When joining a roadway from a private road or driveway, stop and give way to all traffic and pedestrians.

teaching.text: Yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks or at unmarked intersections. When joining a roadway from a private road or driveway, stop and give way to all traffic and pedestrians. Remember: Crossings yield; private entries stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks or at unmarked intersections. When joining a roadway from a private road or driveway, stop and give way to all traffic and pedestrians.

question.text: How does a private-road entry differ from yielding at a pedestrian crossing?

answer.text: At a marked crossing or unmarked intersection, let pedestrians cross. Entry from a private driveway or road adds a required stop before yielding to all traffic and pedestrians.

teaching.text: At a marked crossing or unmarked intersection, let pedestrians cross. Entry from a private driveway or road adds a required stop before yielding to all traffic and pedestrians. Remember: Entry stops; crossings yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a marked crossing or unmarked intersection, let pedestrians cross. Entry from a private driveway or road adds a required stop before yielding to all traffic and pedestrians.

question.text: Who has priority when you make a left turn?

answer.text: When making a left turn after checking that the way is clear, give way to traffic approaching from the opposite direction, including bicycles and pedestrians.

teaching.text: When making a left turn after checking that the way is clear, give way to traffic approaching from the opposite direction, including bicycles and pedestrians. Remember: Left turns yield to opposing traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When making a left turn after checking that the way is clear, give way to traffic approaching from the opposite direction, including bicycles and pedestrians.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Left turns yield to opposing traffic

question.text: What must a left-turning driver yield to when the path otherwise looks clear?

answer.text: Before completing a left turn, allow opposing vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians approaching from that direction to go first.

teaching.text: Before completing a left turn, allow opposing vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians approaching from that direction to go first. Remember: Opposing traffic goes before your left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before completing a left turn, allow opposing vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians approaching from that direction to go first.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Opposing traffic goes before your left

question.text: What must you do before entering from a private road or driveway?

answer.text: Before entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, stop and give way to every vehicle and pedestrian.

teaching.text: Before entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, stop and give way to every vehicle and pedestrian. Remember: Private entry: stop and yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, stop and give way to every vehicle and pedestrian.

question.text: Who proceeds first after simultaneous arrival at an uncontrolled intersection?

answer.text: If vehicles reach an intersection without signs or signals at the same time, the driver on the left gives way to the driver on the right.

teaching.text: If vehicles reach an intersection without signs or signals at the same time, the driver on the left gives way to the driver on the right. Remember: At the same time, right first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If vehicles reach an intersection without signs or signals at the same time, the driver on the left gives way to the driver on the right.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: At the same time, right first

question.text: Which driver yields after simultaneous arrival without signs or signals?

answer.text: At an unsigned, unsignaled intersection reached simultaneously, the driver to the left yields to the driver to the right.

teaching.text: At an unsigned, unsignaled intersection reached simultaneously, the driver to the left yields to the driver to the right. Remember: Left yields to right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At an unsigned, unsignaled intersection reached simultaneously, the driver to the left yields to the driver to the right.

question.text: What crossing duty matters especially when turning on red?

answer.text: Give way to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing in a marked crosswalk or at an unmarked intersection. Red-light turns pose particular danger to pedestrians, so let them cross safely.

teaching.text: Give way to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing in a marked crosswalk or at an unmarked intersection. Red-light turns pose particular danger to pedestrians, so let them cross safely. Remember: Let pedestrians and bicyclists cross safely.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Give way to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing in a marked crosswalk or at an unmarked intersection. Red-light turns pose particular danger to pedestrians, so let them cross safely.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Let pedestrians and bicyclists cross safely

question.text: Why do turns on red require particular attention to crossings?

answer.text: Red-light turns are particularly hazardous for pedestrians. Yield to people walking or cycling across marked crosswalks or unmarked intersections and let them cross safely.

teaching.text: Red-light turns are particularly hazardous for pedestrians. Yield to people walking or cycling across marked crosswalks or unmarked intersections and let them cross safely. Remember: Red turns require crossing vigilance.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Red-light turns are particularly hazardous for pedestrians. Yield to people walking or cycling across marked crosswalks or unmarked intersections and let them cross safely.

question.text: What must you do for an emergency vehicle approaching from behind and for a funeral procession?

answer.text: An emergency vehicle approaching from behind with a siren or flashing lights requires you to yield immediately, pull safely to the right edge and stop until it passes. Give way to funeral processions too.

teaching.text: An emergency vehicle approaching from behind with a siren or flashing lights requires you to yield immediately, pull safely to the right edge and stop until it passes. Give way to funeral processions too. Remember: Emergency behind: right edge and stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An emergency vehicle approaching from behind with a siren or flashing lights requires you to yield immediately, pull safely to the right edge and stop until it passes. Give way to funeral processions too.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Emergency behind: right edge and stop

question.text: How should you pass a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck with flashing lights?

answer.text: Approach a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck with flashing lights cautiously. Change to a nonadjacent lane when reasonable and safe for traffic conditions; if a safe lane change is unavailable, slow down and continue carefully.

teaching.text: Approach a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck with flashing lights cautiously. Change to a nonadjacent lane when reasonable and safe for traffic conditions; if a safe lane change is unavailable, slow down and continue carefully. Remember: Move away safely or slow cautiously.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Approach a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck with flashing lights cautiously. Change to a nonadjacent lane when reasonable and safe for traffic conditions; if a safe lane change is unavailable, slow down and continue carefully.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Move away safely or slow cautiously

question.text: How do active sirens and lights differ from stopped flashers in what they demand?

answer.text: Active sirens and lights demand pulling over, stopping, and waiting, while stopped flashers demand only a lane move or a safe slowdown.

teaching.text: A siren on the move means pull over and stop; lights on a stopped vehicle mean move over or slow. Remember: moving: stop; stopped: move.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Active sirens and lights demand pulling over, stopping, and waiting, while stopped flashers demand only a lane move or a safe slowdown.

question.text: Where must drivers yield to crossing pedestrians and bicyclists?

answer.text: Allow pedestrians and bicyclists to cross safely within marked crosswalks and at unmarked intersections by yielding to them.

teaching.text: Allow pedestrians and bicyclists to cross safely within marked crosswalks and at unmarked intersections by yielding to them. Remember: Marked crosswalks and unmarked intersections.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Allow pedestrians and bicyclists to cross safely within marked crosswalks and at unmarked intersections by yielding to them.

question.text: Which crossing locations require yielding to walkers and bicyclists?

answer.text: Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing at an unmarked intersection or in a marked crosswalk have priority over your vehicle.

teaching.text: Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing at an unmarked intersection or in a marked crosswalk have priority over your vehicle. Remember: Marked or unmarked, crossing priority.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing at an unmarked intersection or in a marked crosswalk have priority over your vehicle.

question.text: How do you enter a roundabout?

answer.text: Enter a roundabout by slowing, yielding to every circulating lane, circling counterclockwise around the island, and yielding to crossing pedestrians.

teaching.text: Slow, yield to every circulating lane and to crossing pedestrians, and go counterclockwise. Remember: slow, yield, counterclockwise.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Enter a roundabout by slowing, yielding to every circulating lane, circling counterclockwise around the island, and yielding to crossing pedestrians.

question.text: How should you position and signal inside a roundabout before exiting?

answer.text: Once inside a roundabout, keep your lane until you are ready to leave, and show your intention with the right turn signal.

teaching.text: Once inside a roundabout, keep your lane until you are ready to leave, and show your intention with the right turn signal. Remember: Keep your lane; signal right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Once inside a roundabout, keep your lane until you are ready to leave, and show your intention with the right turn signal.

question.text: How does entering a roundabout differ from circulating in it?

answer.text: Roundabout entry yields to every circulating lane, while circulating means counterclockwise travel, signed lane choice, and a right-turn exit.

teaching.text: Entering traffic yields to the circle, and the circle runs counterclockwise to a right-turn exit. Remember: enter yields, circle counterclockwise.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Roundabout entry yields to every circulating lane, while circulating means counterclockwise travel, signed lane choice, and a right-turn exit.

question.text: When should you remain in your roundabout lane?

answer.text: Keep your current lane inside a roundabout until you are prepared to exit.

teaching.text: Keep your current lane inside a roundabout until you are prepared to exit. Remember: Keep the lane until exit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep your current lane inside a roundabout until you are prepared to exit.

question.text: What checks and signal precede a lane change?

answer.text: Before moving to another lane, inspect the side and rearview mirrors, signal your intention, and make a quick shoulder glance to check the blind spot just before moving.

teaching.text: Before moving to another lane, inspect the side and rearview mirrors, signal your intention, and make a quick shoulder glance to check the blind spot just before moving. Remember: Mirrors, signal, shoulder glance.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before moving to another lane, inspect the side and rearview mirrors, signal your intention, and make a quick shoulder glance to check the blind spot just before moving.

question.text: What sequence checks mirrors and blind spots before a lane change?

answer.text: Check mirrors for approaching traffic, signal your lane change, then make a brief shoulder check for a vehicle in the blind spot before moving.

teaching.text: Check mirrors for approaching traffic, signal your lane change, then make a brief shoulder check for a vehicle in the blind spot before moving. Remember: Check, signal, glance, then move.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Check mirrors for approaching traffic, signal your lane change, then make a brief shoulder check for a vehicle in the blind spot before moving.

question.text: When can you return to the right lane after passing?

answer.text: After overtaking, move back to the right once your interior rearview mirror shows the front of the vehicle you passed.

teaching.text: After overtaking, move back to the right once your interior rearview mirror shows the front of the vehicle you passed. Remember: See the passed vehicle front.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After overtaking, move back to the right once your interior rearview mirror shows the front of the vehicle you passed.

question.text: Where is passing unlawful, and what same-direction lane exception applies?

answer.text: Passing on hills or curves, or at intersections or railway crossings, is unlawful except on roads offering at least two traffic lanes going in the same direction.

teaching.text: Passing on hills or curves, or at intersections or railway crossings, is unlawful except on roads offering at least two traffic lanes going in the same direction. Remember: Hills, curves, crossings; multi-lane exception.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing on hills or curves, or at intersections or railway crossings, is unlawful except on roads offering at least two traffic lanes going in the same direction.

question.text: What clearance and location rules govern returning after a pass and prohibited passing?

answer.text: After overtaking, move back right once your rearview mirror shows the front of the vehicle you passed. Passing is barred on hills, curves, at intersections and at railroad crossings unless the road provides two or more lanes traveling your way. Do not pass a school bus stopped to pick up or discharge passengers on a public road, except when a physical barrier or an unpaved median divides opposing traffic. The prohibition also covers a bus stopped to pick up or discharge passengers on a private road.

teaching.text: After overtaking, move back right once your rearview mirror shows the front of the vehicle you passed. Passing is barred on hills, curves, at intersections and at railroad crossings unless the road provides two or more lanes traveling your way. Do not pass a school bus stopped to pick up or discharge passengers on a public road, except when a physical barrier or an unpaved median divides opposing traffic. The prohibition also covers a bus stopped to pick up or discharge passengers on a private road. Remember: Front visible; check passing prohibitions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After overtaking, move back right once your rearview mirror shows the front of the vehicle you passed. Passing is barred on hills, curves, at intersections and at railroad crossings unless the road provides two or more lanes traveling your way. Do not pass a school bus stopped to pick up or discharge passengers on a public road, except when a physical barrier or an unpaved median divides opposing traffic. The prohibition also covers a bus stopped to pick up or discharge passengers on a private road.

question.text: What does a solid line on the left of your lane mean for passing?

answer.text: Passing is forbidden when the line immediately to the left of your lane is solid.

teaching.text: Passing is forbidden when the line immediately to the left of your lane is solid. Remember: Solid left line: no passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing is forbidden when the line immediately to the left of your lane is solid.

question.text: What location and zone boundaries restrict passing?

answer.text: Do not pass on hills or curves, or at intersections or railway crossings, except where at least two lanes run in your direction. Finish overtaking before reaching a No Passing zone.

teaching.text: Do not pass on hills or curves, or at intersections or railway crossings, except where at least two lanes run in your direction. Finish overtaking before reaching a No Passing zone. Remember: Location exception; finish before the zone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not pass on hills or curves, or at intersections or railway crossings, except where at least two lanes run in your direction. Finish overtaking before reaching a No Passing zone.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Location exception; finish before the zone
